strings.Decomp Buddy has no investors, no ads, a: Decomp Buddy has no investors, no ads, and no plan to get any. It has a tip page. You can probably see where this is going.
strings.Decomp Buddy is free. There is no paywal: Decomp Buddy is free. There is no paywall coming, no account to make, and no advertising. You bring your own AI key and your own legally owned games; nothing about you leaves this computer. If it saved you an evening of README archaeology, you can support Maddie's work, and that support is what keeps her building useful, privacy-respecting things the world forgot to make.
strings.Decomp Buddy is one of those holes. The: Decomp Buddy is one of those holes. The decomp and recomp scene is doing something remarkable - turning games that were locked to old consoles into real native PC programs - but every project ships with its own build, its own folder rules, its own idea of where your disc image goes. Maddie got tired of reading twenty READMEs to set up twenty games, so she built the thing that reads them for you, checks that the dump you picked is the one the project actually wants, and hands you a folder that just works.
strings.Decomp Buddy never downloads games. You: Decomp Buddy never downloads games. You supply your own copies; verification checks they're the ones the project needs.
